I'm tracing why "flag" being required and missing triggers the loop correctly: since self.required already contained "flag" directly (not via gather_requires), the previous call computed req_args as "flag" and "opt" properly, with used empty since no args were passed—explaining why it worked before without the inclusion logic.

But this simple single-required-arg case isn't where the bug lives; the real issue is the ArgGroup scenario, where "first" is required via gather_requires but somehow gets filtered out of req_args despite being in self.required. I'm digging through the debug trace for get_required_usage_from to see where unrolled_reqs still contains "first" yet the final req_args ends up empty—tracing through the incls, matcher state, and unroll_arg calls to pinpoint where it drops out.

I found it: the arg-loop filters out any name that appears in args_in_groups, which is built from unrolling the required group "either_or_both" into its members [first, second]. Since "first" is a member of that required group, it gets excluded from the arg-loop entirely on the assumption the group listing will cover it—that's the root cause of it going missing.

But then in the groups loop, "either_or_both" checks if any of its members is already present, and since "second" is present, it skips adding the group name too. So neither the individual "first" nor the group "either_or_both" ends up in ret_val, leaving it empty.

The real bug is that args_in_groups filtering shouldn't suppress an arg just because it belongs to a group—it should only suppress it when the requirement actually stems from the group itself, not from an unrelated `requires()` relationship triggered by another present arg.

Given the pr4006 reference, I suspect the actual upstream fix passes an explicit "incls" list into missing_required_error and has get_required_usage_from merge that in directly, rather than trying to fix the group-filtering logic itself.

I realize simply passing incl won't work since the filter still excludes anything already in args_in_groups. I need to adjust that filter so incls are allowed through even when they're part of args_in_groups, though this only helps if incls actually contains the arg id being checked.

Then I reconsider: adding arg.id to incl unconditionally at line 486 could break other call sites where "used" status matters for usage-line formatting, even though tests passed before my edit. So the fix should only add the arg to incl when it's actually being filtered out due to args_in_groups membership, rather than doing it universally for the simple required-arg case.

Actually maybe the better fix is to leave missing_required_error's incl untouched and instead correct the root cause in get_required_usage_from: an arg shouldn't be excluded from individual listing just because it's in a satisfied group, if that arg is also directly in self.required. I'm now tracing why "first" ends up in unrolled_reqs/self.required in the first place -- it's likely added there because gather_requires pulls it in through a require-first relationship, making it a direct requirement rather than just a group-derived one.

The real fix should be to only exclude an arg from individual listing if the group covering it is actually satisfied and skipped, not simply because it belongs to some group. I want to restructure so the group loop determines which groups remain unsatisfied first, then only those groups' args get excluded from the individual arg listing—rather than filtering based on group membership alone.
